One roll, five steps

// 05 frames //
FILMTRAIL 400 ▸ 1

Meter the light

Uses the phone's light sensor, the same way an incident meter reads the light falling on your subject.

  • Aperture or shutter priority, EV compensation
  • Set ISO from your film
  • Per-phone calibration against a meter you trust
FILMTRAIL 400 ▸ 2

Log every frame

Tap once right after the shutter. FilmTrail keeps the time, the GPS position and the exposure you used.

  • Hold to add a voice note
  • Optional small reference picture of the scene
  • Quick Settings tile and home screen widget
FILMTRAIL 400 ▸ 3

Match your scans

Pick the scanned files, frame by frame, with the voice note and reference picture to remind you which is which.

  • Writes GPS into the EXIF of a copy
  • Pixels are never re-encoded
  • JPEG and PNG
FILMTRAIL 400 ▸ 4

See the trail

Every frame on a map with its thumbnail. Tap a pin to see the photo and the frame's details.

  • Map pins with thumbnails
  • Show one roll or all of them
  • Backup file to move to a new phone
FILMTRAIL 400 ▸ 5

Take it further

Share a roll's log in formats other map apps and spreadsheets open, and see each frame where you shot it.

  • GPX for Organic Maps and OsmAnd
  • KMZ for Google Earth and Google My Maps, with your photos as pins
  • CSV for Excel or Google Sheets
Privacy

Your trail stays with you.

No account, no ads, no analytics. Rolls, frames, locations and voice notes are stored only on your phone.

Questions

Is it free?

Yes. FilmTrail is free, with no ads and no in-app purchases.

Does it work offline?

Yes. Metering, logging and matching work without a connection. Only the map background needs the internet, and you can leave it off.

Which cameras?

Any film camera, 35 mm or medium format. FilmTrail doesn't talk to the camera; you tap the phone after each shot.

iPhone?

Not for now. FilmTrail is Android only (Android 8.0 and later).

Load the next roll.
